title: Post Intensive Care Syndrome (PICS) in patients after coronary artery bypass graft surgery
summary:
The CritCABG study examines how often Post-Intensive Care Syndrome (PICS) occurs after planned bypass surgery and what factors contribute to its development. In Germany, around 50,000 such operations are performed each year. Many patients spend several days in intensive care, and about 40% require extended treatment. While survival rates for older and critically ill patients are improving, the long-term effects on their independence and quality of life remain a major challenge. PICS is a complex condition that can cause psychological symptoms (e.g., anxiety or depression), memory problems, and physical weakness. These symptoms can last for years but are often not detected or treated in time. Moreover, structured follow-up programs for ICU survivors are not widely available. One potential cause of PICS is inflammation, triggered by substances called cytokines, which are released in the body during and after surgery. The CritCABG study investigates how these inflammatory processes are linked to PICS development.

The study collects data from two perspectives:
- Retrospectively, researchers analyze how many patients develop PICS after bypass surgery and how it affects their daily lives.
- Prospectively, they examine which inflammatory markers and risk factors might contribute to PICS.

The goal is to develop better prevention and treatment strategies for PICS and to raise awareness of this important health issue.
conditions: Post Intensive Care Syndrom after coronary artery bypass graft surgery (OPS-2025: 5-36)

interventions.name: Observational study, retrospective study arm: Retrospective assessment of PICS-typical symptoms after bypass surgery.

Observational study, prospective study arm: Prospective assessment of PICS symptoms, risk factors, and cytokine profile before, during, and after the intensive care unit stay in the context of bypass surgery. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Intensive care init stay after coronary artery bypass graft surgery (OPS Code 5-36 – Coronary Vessel Procedures, 2014–2024), voluntary participation, written informed consent after consultation, sufficient German language proficiency.
Exclusion criteria:
Inability to provide informed consent (due to linguistic, psychological, or somatic reasons), employees involved in the study or their relatives, withdrawal of consent (secondary exclusion criterion). 

Additional exclusion criteria for the prospective study arm: Pre-existing or suspected polyneuropathy/myopathy, prior immobilization (defined as being bedridden for more than 50% of the day over a period of two weeks)
